en: Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines, standing at exactly 2,954 meters above sea level.
Taal Volcano in Batangas is the smallest active volcano in the world, standing only 311 meters above sea level.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering a surface area of approximately 911 square kilometers.
Mount Pulag is the highest mountain in Luzon and the third highest in the Philippines, reaching 2,928 meters.
The Philippine Sea is a marginal sea of the Western Pacific Ocean, covering an estimated area of five million square kilometers.
The Philippine eagle is one of the largest eagles in the world, featuring a wingspan of up to two meters.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River features a navigable underground river stretching 8.2 kilometers long directly into the sea.
Baguio City receives an average annual rainfall of over 3,800 millimeters, making it one of the wettest cities in the Philippines.
Palawan is the largest province in the Philippines by land area, covering roughly 14,649 square kilometers.
The Sierra Madre mountain range is the longest in the Philippines, extending approximately 540 kilometers along the eastern coast of Luzon.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of at least 1,268 perfectly cone-shaped hills spread over an area of more than 50 square kilometers.
